newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Brazil's Maciel rules out devaluation of real.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Maciel rules out devaluation of real.

text.p: Brazilian Vice-President Marco Maciel ruled out Tuesday reports of a planned devaluation of the real against the dollar in March.
"We are not considering nor have we considered any alteration in our exchange rate policy," Maciel told a news conference in a three-day official visit to Paraguay.
"We understand the real plan is a very successful plan through which we not only have a stable exchange rate, but also sustainable development," Maciel said.
He was responding to a question about Paraguayan media reports that Brazil was planning a March devaluation to spur faster economic growth.
"We now have sustainable, organic growth which is not based on inflationary mechanisms," Maciel said.
He is due to stay in Paraguay until Wednesday. A prime reason for his visit is to promote business with Brazil's poor northeast.
Brazil and Paraguay, along with Argentina and Uruguay, are members of the Mercosur customs union.
